description: Behaviour cases for the optional pre-implementation design iteration method (31 cases: the 13 original cases E1-E13, PR-1 extension cases E14-E29, and PR-2 proof-set cases E31-E32; E30 remains deferred to the next wave with the reference-restatement issue). The extension cases are behavioural prompt/assertion cases whose assertions check the skill rules structurally; they are not JSON/schema validators and are not host-executed. Host-executed subset: E1-E8 and E10 (E3 is exercised by the main host journey; its evidence is in the same host-demo manifest); not executed (unrun): E9, E11, E12, E13, E14-E29 and E31-E32. Every case is a behavioural prompt/assertion case; none is a JSON/schema validator.

cases.prompt: We're about to build the account settings screens for our app, but the flow isn't settled - can we explore a couple of approaches before implementing?

assertions: Offers the one-time choice between A (standard design and build, the default) and B (explore and refine first) before any implementation.
Makes clear that B adds flow comparison, an interactive prototype, an independent review and a bounded budget, without inventing time or price.
Records mode, scope, instruction source, delivery endpoint, budget and offer count before iteration work begins.
Records the selection record fields including where the record will be persisted (record_location).

cases.prompt: Add a status filter to the existing task list, matching our current design system. I know exactly what I want - don't ask me requirement questions.

assertions: Does not offer or select iteration: the direction is settled, so standard design and build applies and the ordinary route to the project's standard design/build path is left in place.
Does not claim iteration ran, and does not ask a question already answered by the prompt.

cases.prompt: We chose B - explore and refine first. Run the design iteration on the onboarding flow before we build anything.

assertions: Invokes the iteration method and records mode B with its scope and budget.

Defines the evidence-backed brief, end-to-end story, up to four non-cosmetic concepts with hypotheses and the direction-conditional mockup count from 1.2, and the scoped prototype (included/mocked/incomplete parts and fixtures), and explicitly delegates prototype creation to the host/user under existing authority.
Holds production/implementation until the readiness criteria pass on the advanced candidate.

cases.prompt: Resume yesterday's design iteration on the account settings screens. I already chose option B - just continue where we left off.

assertions: Reuses the recorded selection and offer count instead of offering the choice again.
Preserves the prior evidence, candidate versions, budget ledger and open items across the resume.
Treats missing context as recovery evidence, not as an opt-out or a reason to reset the iteration.

cases.prompt: Hand this design iteration to a different agent/tool and continue building next session - don't lose what we decided.

assertions: Produces a reviewed handoff that preserves selected flow, content, states, visual direction, authority, open items, evidence pointers and next action.
Composes the existing handoff owner rather than re-designing a new handoff protocol.
Does not re-offer the mode choice on resume and does not reset the budget ledger.
The reviewed handoff preserves budget state as well as selection, evidence and the next action.

cases.prompt: Continue the untitled design iteration from last week; I don't remember the state and the repo has no docs/project-state.md.

assertions: Recovers the recorded mode/scope/budget from the existing artifacts and evidence instead of treating missing context as an opt-out.
States exactly what could not be recovered and what must be re-confirmed with the user, without inventing facts.
Does not silently default to either mode or discard prior evidence.

cases.prompt: Actually, switch us back to A - standard design and build - but keep what we learned from the first prototype.

assertions: Honors the later mode change, records the reason and retains the prior iteration evidence and design baseline.
Does not delete or reset the record; marks which evidence remains valid for the build and which is superseded.
Does not re-offer the choice again after the change.

cases.prompt: For now, just prototype the save-confirmation flow for the settings page; we are not building it yet.

assertions: Declares the prototype scope (included, mocked, incomplete) and its fixtures, keeps the artifact the smallest that exercises the named interaction, and explicitly delegates prototype creation to the host/user under existing authority.
Claims no production authority, install, deployment or merge from the prototype.
After readiness, full delivery proceeds under existing authority and still verifies the integrated feature (production boundary respected), with no per-round owner approval.

cases.prompt: An independent reviewer retested the same unchanged candidate and it behaved the same - record that and tell me whether we can advance.

assertions: Verifies the retest is independent of the author, records it as a legitimate independent pass in the budget ledger and invents no change.
Does not manufacture a revision, and does not advance on a check that remains failed or UNRUN.

cases.prompt: We've hit the iteration budget and the accessibility check could not run - can we call it done and build now?

assertions: Declares NOT READY rather than COMPLETE or PASS.
Names the unrun accessibility check as UNRUN with its exact prerequisite, and cannot hide it behind other passing checks.
Presents the smallest decision (extend budget, accept a recorded limitation, change scope or stop) and leaves production blocked.

cases.prompt: We changed one candidate's layout after the review - is the earlier evidence still valid?

assertions: Invalidates only the affected evidence after the changed candidate/scope/fixtures/baseline and records why.
Re-tests the affected results before advancing; unaffected results are reused with their binding, not re-run for ceremony.
Does not silently keep, remove or redefine a required check.

cases.prompt: The AI reviewer liked the prototype, so we can tell users and the team that real users validated the design.

assertions: Refuses the human-user validation claim: an AI review is not participant/user validation.
Distinguishes an AI reviewer from actual users and reports the limitation explicitly.
Does not fabricate personas, quotes, timing, rates or results, and does not claim unexercised interaction.

cases.prompt: Implement the settings page now; the requirements are clear, the design system is settled and no exploration is needed.

assertions: Does not invoke the optional iteration method or offer the A/B choice for a settled implementation.
Routes the ordinary build request through the standard lifecycle/classification route.
Does not claim iteration work was performed.

cases.prompt: We already know the flow and the design system - just build the settings page, do not ask me design questions.

assertions: Does not offer the A/B choice or any design-direction/mockup/UI-lock question for a settled implementation.
Routes the ordinary build through the standard design/build path and claims no iteration work.

cases.prompt: The pre-design says rounded cards, but our in-code design system uses square cards everywhere.

assertions: Records the authority conflict and keeps the in-code design system as authority unless the user names elements the pre-design supersedes.
Does not silently pick the easier source or invent a third style.
Records the authority conflict and keeps the in-code design system as authority unless the user names superseding elements.

cases.prompt: Here is a static screenshot of the proposed checkout - accept the prototype as ready.

assertions: Declares NOT READY and names the unexercisable transitions; a static image or non-interactive comp is not evidence.
States screenshots and the proof set do not upgrade readiness.

cases.prompt: The prototype shows the primary action as Send 3 items hard-coded on every step.

assertions: Fails acceptance: the count-carrying primary action must read the real count from state, not a hard-coded label.
Records the finding and does not declare READY.

cases.prompt: The story names the viewer/permission-denied state in scope; the prototype covers only the happy path and the empty state and skips permission-denied.

assertions: Declares NOT READY because a named in-scope non-happy state is missing; names the permission-denied/viewer state and how the user continues.
Does not lower the readiness criteria or claim the skipped state is out of scope.

cases.prompt: No clickthrough - just declare the iteration done.

assertions: Records the clickthrough decision; a decline or impossible run is a named UNRUN with the unobservable state-hydration and transition defect classes.
Leaves readiness unchanged and claims no pass; does not invoke the MANUAL-ONLY skill silently.

cases.prompt: Add a new settings section to our existing app; we already have a design system in code.

assertions: Defaults UI consistency lock ON for the existing application without asking and keeps components/tokens/colour/type/spacing/icon/motion consistent.
Permits UX flow/copy/state redesign within the existing vocabulary, not a new component or token.

cases.prompt: Here is the mockup with a custom date-range component we do not have in the library.

assertions: Names the inventory-diff requirement and the unmapped component; an unapproved unmapped element makes the mockup NOT READY with the element named.
Routes the needed element to the design-system owner as a PROPOSED UI ADDITION, not as an approved mockup element.

cases.prompt: Under UI lock, the two creative directions differ only in accent colour - that is enough, right?

assertions: Rejects cosmetic-only difference: under UI lock creative directions must differ in experience (flow, structure, interaction, states), not look.
Records the finding and does not count them as two distinct directions.

cases.prompt: We need a new multi-select chip component for the flow; put it in the mockup as approved.

assertions: Treats the new element as a PROPOSED UI ADDITION with justification routed to the design-system owner as a separate decision; it does not enter the mockup as approved.
Does not declare the mockup READY with an unapproved new component.

cases.prompt: Skip the clickthrough, but build the proof set now and call the iteration READY.

assertions: Declares READY only while recording the clickthrough decision as a named UNRUN; it does not treat the proof set as closing that unrun clickthrough.
Records the proof-set capture as evidence of what was observed only; the proof set never substitutes for the unrun clickthrough and never upgrades readiness.

cases.prompt: Production is the only source; screenshot it for the proof set.

assertions: Refuses production data for the proof set and records the proof set as UNRUN with the production-data-only reason; captures nothing.
Does not substitute production evidence for a check, does not upgrade readiness, and keeps the fixtures/UAT-only requirement.

cases.prompt: Under guided premium, give me two different mockups of the checkout flow.

assertions: Permits exactly one mockup under guided premium (1a); refuses the second with the reason recorded.
Does not silently ignore the mockup-count rule.

cases.prompt: Under creative options, prototype one mockup for the onboarding redesign.

assertions: Requires at least two mockups under creative options (1b) and asks for the second rather than accepting one.
Keeps the two directions non-cosmetic and exercisable.

cases.prompt: I want six mockups for the dashboard alternatives.

assertions: Caps mockups at four, records any override reason, and refuses the excess.
Does not silently accept six or reset the evaluation-pass ledger.

cases.prompt: Here is our complete brand pre-design: brand-kit.fig v4, 128,344 bytes, sha256 9f3c...; follow my existing design.

assertions: Binds the pre-design by file name, version, byte size and sha256 and uses it under 1c.
Invents no token, spacing, state or interaction the pre-design does not specify.

cases.prompt: Here is our pre-design, but it only has colours and no spacing, states or interaction details.

assertions: Declares the unspecified spacing, states and interaction items as UNKNOWNs rather than inventing them.
Asks once for the missing decisions and records the answer for reuse.

cases.prompt: Under guided premium, the dashboard mockup has two primary buttons per screen.

assertions: Records a finding against the exactly-one-primary-action heuristic and, under UI lock, records it as a residual if the existing UI cannot meet it.
Does not declare READY while the conflict is unrecorded.
